arxiv-2105-05491.title: Continuity of measure-dimension mappings Thanks: The work is supported by ZR2019QA003 from SPNSF and 12001056 from NSFC
arxiv-2105-05491.creator: Liangang Ma
arxiv-2105-05491.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Liangang Ma. We study continuity and discontinuity of the upper and lower (modified) box-counting, Hausdorff, packing, (modified) correlation measure-dimension mappings under the weak, setwise and TV topology on the space of Borel measures respectively in this work. We give various examples to show that no continuity can be guaranteed under the weak, setwise or TV topology on the space of Borel measures for any of these measure-dimension mappings.

arxiv-2201-02585.title: Sub-surface granular dynamics in the context of oblique, low-velocity impacts into angular granular media
arxiv-2201-02585.creator: Peter M. Miklavčič, Paul Sánchez, Esteban Wright, Alice C. Quillen, Hesam Askari
arxiv-2201-02585.description: Abstract Oblique, low-velocity impacts onto non-terrestrial terrain are regular occurrences during space exploration missions. These are not only a necessary component of landing and sampling maneuvers, but can also be used as impact experiments to reveal characteristics of the interacting surfaces. We conduct two-dimensional discrete simulations to model such impacts into a bed of triangular grains.

arxiv-2205-14348.title: Exponential mixing and limit theorems of quasi-periodically forced 2D stochastic Navier-Stokes Equations in the hypoelliptic setting
arxiv-2205-14348.creator: Rongchang Liu, Kening Lu
arxiv-2205-14348.description: Abstract . We consider the incompressible 2D Navier-Stokes equations on the torus driven by a deterministic time quasi-periodic force and a noise that is white in time and degenerate in Fourier space. We show that the asymptotic statistical behavior is characterized by a quasi-periodic invariant measure that exponentially attracts the law of all solutions.

arxiv-2212-09434.title: Quasi-parametric rates for Sparse Multivariate Functional Principal Components Analysis
arxiv-2212-09434.creator: Ryad Belhakem
arxiv-2212-09434.description: Abstract This work aims to give non-asymptotic results for estimating the first principal component of a multivariate random process. We first define the covariance function and the covariance operator in the multivariate case. We then define a projection operator. This operator can be seen as a reconstruction step from the raw data in the functional data analysis context.

arxiv-2309-12242.title: Weakly-supervised Automated Audio Captioning via text only training
arxiv-2309-12242.description: Abstract In recent years, datasets of paired audio and captions have enabled remarkable success in automatically generating descriptions for audio clips, namely Automated Audio Captioning (AAC). However, it is labor-intensive and time-consuming to collect a sufficient number of paired audio and captions.

arxiv-2401-05300.title: I am a Strange Dataset: Metalinguistic Tests for Language Models
arxiv-2401-05300.creator: Tristan Thrush, Jared Moore, Miguel Monares, Christopher Potts, Douwe Kiela § \mathsection Stanford University; † \dagger UC San Diego; ‡ \ddagger Playtest AI; ¶ \mathparagraph Contextual AI tthrush@stanford.edu
arxiv-2401-05300.description: Abstract Statements involving metalinguistic self-reference (“This paper has six sections.”) are prevalent in many domains. Can current large language models (LLMs) handle such language? In this paper, we present “I am a Strange Dataset”, a new dataset for addressing this question. There are two subtasks: generation and verification .

arxiv-2503-04458.title: Quantum energies of solitons with different topological charges
arxiv-2503-04458.creator: N. Graham a) , H. Weigel b)
arxiv-2503-04458.description: Abstract The vacuum polarization energy is the leading quantum correction to the classical energy of a soliton. We study this energy for two-component solitons in one space dimension as a function of the soliton’s topological charge. We find that both the classical and the vacuum polarization energies are linear functions of the topological charge with a small offset.

arxiv-2504-02297.title: The temperature dependence of fractional topological charge objects
arxiv-2504-02297.creator: Derek B. Leinweber
arxiv-2504-02297.description: Abstract We present a novel method for defining the topological charge contained within distinct topological objects in the nontrivial ground-state fields of SU ⁡ ( N ) \mathrm{SU}(N) lattice gauge theory. Such an analysis has been called for by the growing number of models for Yang-Mills topological structure which propose the existence of fractionally charged objects.

arxiv-2508-14913.title: Bridging the Culture Gap : A Framework for LLM-Driven Socio-Cultural Localization of Math Word Problems in Low-Resource Languages
arxiv-2508-14913.creator: Israel Abebe Azime, Tadesse Destaw Belay, Dietrich Klakow, Philipp Slusallek, Anshuman Chhabra
arxiv-2508-14913.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated significant capabilities in solving mathematical problems expressed in natural language. However, multilingual and culturally-grounded mathematical reasoning in low-resource languages lags behind English due to the scarcity of socio-cultural task datasets that reflect accurate native entities such as person names, organization names, and currencies.

pmc-10741847.title: Platelet Counts and Risk of Severe Retinopathy of Prematurity: A Bayesian Model-Averaged Meta-Analysis
pmc-10741847.creator: Mohamad F Almutairi, Silvia Gulden, Tamara M Hundscheid, František Bartoš, Giacomo Cavallaro, Eduardo Villamor, Stefan Grosek
pmc-10741847.description: Background: We aimed to conduct a systematic review and Bayesian model-averaged meta-analysis (BMA) on the association between platelet counts and severe retinopathy of prematurity (ROP). Methods: We searched for studies reporting on platelet counts (continuous variable) or thrombocytopenia (categorical variable) and severe ROP or aggressive posterior ROP (APROP).

pmc-11347826.title: Utility of interim apparent diffusion coefficient value in predicting treatment response among patients with locally advanced cervical cancer treated with radiotherapy
pmc-11347826.creator: Chunyu Liang, Wei Wang, Guohui Yang, Zhiyuan Xu, Jian Li, Kusheng Wu, Xinping Shen
pmc-11347826.description: Highlights•This research investigated the utility of pre-treatment, interim-ADC as well as change in ADC for predicting treatment outcomes in patients with cervical carcinoma treated with radiotherapy.•Multivariate logistic regression revealed that the baseline tumor diameter and interim-ADC were significant prognostic factors for treatment response.•Interim-ADC value may serve as a novel imaging marker for predicting the outcomes of therapy.

pmc-11478951.title: Optimal Design of a Sensor Network for Guided Wave-Based Structural Health Monitoring Using Acoustically Coupled Optical Fibers
pmc-11478951.creator: Rohan Soman, Jee Myung Kim, Alex Boyer, Kara Peters
pmc-11478951.description: Guided waves (GW) allow fast inspection of a large area and hence have received great interest from the structural health monitoring (SHM) community. Fiber Bragg grating (FBG) sensors offer several advantages but their use has been limited for the GW sensing due to its limited sensitivity.

pmc-11591045.title: Expert Consultation: Factors Influencing End-of-Life Decision-Making for Dairy Cattle Across the United States Supply Chain
pmc-11591045.creator: Lily Edwards-Callaway, Brianna McBride, Erica Machuca, Lauren Dean, Kira Sayre, Catie Cramer, Noa Román-Muñiz, Kayleigh Keller, Lorann Stallones, Diego Manriquez
pmc-11591045.description: Simple SummaryMaking end-of-life decisions for dairy cattle (i.e., euthanasia and fitness for transport) is a complex topic with a significant impact on dairy cattle welfare and the sustainability of the entire dairy supply chain. In this study, experts serving supportive roles in the dairy industry identified factors that influence end-of-life decision-making for dairy cattle.

pmc-11667720.title: Generation of Quaternary Carbons in Cycloalkanones and Lactones with Arynes through a Domino Process
pmc-11667720.creator: Jih Ru Hwu, Khagendra Prasad Bohara, Mohit Kapoor, Animesh Roy, Shu-Yu Lin, Chun-Cheng Lin, Kuo-Chu Hwang, Wen-Chieh Huang, Shwu-Chen Tsay
pmc-11667720.description: A synthetic method was developed for the generation of a quaternary carbon center in carbonyl compounds. This innovative process involved the reaction of α-thiolate lactones and cycloalkanones with two equivalents of arynes in acetonitrile to give α,α-diarylated products in 63–85% yields at 25 °C.

pmc-12608827.title: Ovariectomy Induces Selective Alterations in Dura Mater Blood and Lymphatic Microvascular Network Architecture in Mice
pmc-12608827.creator: Olga V Glinskii, Imad Eddine Toubal, Leike Xie, Sunilima Sinha, Kannappan Palaniappan, Vladislav V Glinsky, Pablo Martín-Vasallo
pmc-12608827.description: Ovarian hormones are essential regulators of vascular homeostasis, yet their deficiency’s effects on the meningeal microvasculature remain incompletely understood. We used high-resolution imaging to assess the cranial dura mater (CDM) blood and lymphatic microvasculature in ovariectomized (OVX) and control (intact or sham-operated) mice, followed by morphometric analysis of microvessel architecture.

pmc-12748811.title: Mechanisms for agricultural companies in enabling smallholders’ integration into modern agriculture
pmc-12748811.creator: Yakun Chen, Hongzhen Zhang, Yuchen Lu, Zhijie Song
pmc-12748811.description: Smallholder articulation of modern agriculture is an important foundation for the realization of agricultural modernization, and in the context of the market playing a decisive role in resource allocation, can agricultural companies with market advantages promote smallholder articulation of modern agricultural production?

pmc-12812718.title: Exploration of CDIO-based training mode with a sequential teaching approach for emergency department novice nurses
pmc-12812718.creator: Chen Lin, Qianqian Jin, Xiu Huang, Dejun Liao
pmc-12812718.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesTo evaluate a CDIO-based sequential tutorial system for emergency-department (ED) novice nurses.MethodsForty novice nurses (nine male, 31 female; mean age 21.4 ± 0.9 years; predominantly bachelor’s degree holders) rotating in the ED were allocated by time period to either a CDIO group (n = 18, September 2022 to June 2023) or a traditional-tutorial group (n = 22, September 2021 to June 2022) for a 3-month program. Both groups received equal training hours.

pmc-12858114.title: Difference in blood pressure levels in patients with hypertension with and without refillable prescription program in family medicine
pmc-12858114.creator: Brian González-Pérez, Rebeca Benítez Torres, Francisco C. Martínez, Raúl de León Escobedo, Ricardo Salas Flores, Alma A. Peña Maldonado
pmc-12858114.description: Arterial hypertension (AHT) is a chronic disease characterized by persistently elevated blood pressure levels in the arteries. The reported prevalence of AHT in Mexico is 31.5%. Due to the multiple complications that uncontrolled AHT can cause, it is necessary for healthcare personnel to manage this condition professionally.

pmc-12983728.title: Antibiotic use among patients admitted to tertiary hospitals in Uganda: a trend analysis of 2020–2023 point prevalence surveys
pmc-12983728.creator: Suzan Nakasendwa, Jonathan Mayito, Vivian Twemanye, Conrad Tumwine, Reuben Kiggundu, Ronald Galiwango, Elly Nuwamanya, James Muleme, Flavia Dhikusooka, Herman Mwanja, Ellon Twinomuhwezi, Harriet Akello, Morries Seru, Hope Mackline, Dathan M Byonanebye, Francis Kakooza, Andrew Kambugu
pmc-12983728.description: ObjectiveLimited data exist on temporal changes in antibiotic use in low and middle-income countries. We evaluated trends in antibiotic use at tertiary hospitals in Uganda.DesignRetrospective trend analysis of a repeated point prevalence survey (PPS).Setting and participantsThis study utilised antibiotic use data from quarterly PPS conducted among inpatients at nine regional referral hospitals in Uganda between October 2020 and December 2023.

pmc-13179715.title: Triple Trouble: Early Clues in the Diagnosis of Allgrove Syndrome: A Case Report
pmc-13179715.creator: Titilope Majiyagbe, Anitha Kumaran, Lawrence Gnanaraj, Claire Wood, Kalyani Sen
pmc-13179715.description: IntroductionAllgrove syndrome (also known as Triple A syndrome) is an inherited autosomal recessive condition, characterised by achalasia, alacrima and adrenal insufficiency. Its rarity and high phenotypic heterogeneity mean that it often poses a diagnostic challenge.Case PresentationWe discuss the case of a previously well 5‐year‐old who presented with adrenal crisis.

pmc-13264958.title: Ultra-processed food and risk of gastric cancer: a systematic review
pmc-13264958.creator: Abdur Rahman, Tahmid Hussain, Munia Afroz, Sakib Rahman, Malay Kanti Mridha, Abu Ahmed Shamim, Fahmida Akter
pmc-13264958.description: IntroductionUltra-processed food (UPF) consumption has increased globally and has been linked to several non-communicable diseases including cancer. However, evidence regarding its association with gastric cancer (GC) remains limited and inconsistent. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the association between UPF consumption and GC risk.

pmc-13414528.title: Regional and Seasonal Dynamics of Leptospirosis in Ukraine, 2023–2025
pmc-13414528.creator: Pavlo Petakh, Iryna Halabitska, Oleh Lushchak, Oleksandr Kamyshnyi
pmc-13414528.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Ukraine has substantial regional differences in climate, landscape, forest cover, and river networks, which may influence leptospirosis transmission. However, recent monthly oblast-level variation in leptospirosis incidence has not been systematically described. We used newly available surveillance data for 2023–2025 to assess seasonal and regional patterns of leptospirosis and their associations with weather, climatic zone, forest cover, and river network density. Methods: We analyzed surveillance data from 23 Ukrainian oblasts. Incidence was assessed by month, oblast, and climatic zone.

pmc-13543835.title: Cr(VI) and DON co-exposure triggers intestinal epithelial cells ferroptosis and pyroptosis through Nrf2/NF-κB/NLRP3 to impair intestinal barrier function
pmc-13543835.creator: Yueming Gu, Xinyuan Miao, Linrui Fan, Guodong Cai, Ruilong Song, Hui Zou, Jianhong Gu, Yan Yuan, Xuezhong Liu, Zongping Liu, Jianchun Bian
pmc-13543835.description: Objectives Cr(VI) and DON are natural co-occurring pollutants in the environment. This study aimed to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying oxidative damage to the intestinal barrier and intestinal epithelial cell (IECs) toxicity induced by Cr(VI) and DON.MethodsThe target genes and signaling pathways were predicted using the network toxicology method.

pmc-13622444.title: Quality of life with nivolumab and AVD first‐line treatment of Hodgkin lymphoma in the Phase II GHSG NIVAHL trial
pmc-13622444.creator: Christian Peter Jaworek, Ina Bühnen, Peter Herhaus, Julia Meissner, Karolin Trautmann‐Grill, Teresa Halbsguth, Andrea Kerkhoff, Valdete Schaub, Michael Fuchs, Bastian von Tresckow, Peter Borchmann, Karolin Behringer

pmc-13650225.title: Bimekizumab as an Effective Treatment in Darier Disease: Clinical Outcomes of a Single-Center Retrospective Analysis of Patients Treated with Biologics
pmc-13650225.creator: David L. Ranzinger, Paul Schmidle, Matthias Seifert, Sophia Wasserer, Kristin Technau-Hafsi, Cristina Has, Kilian Eyerich, Anna C. Pilz
pmc-13650225.description: IntroductionDarier disease (DD) is a rare autosomal dominant genodermatosis with limited systemic therapeutic options. Retinoids are the gold standard therapy, but long-term application is frequently limited by adverse events. Case reports suggest that biologicals approved for psoriasis vulgaris or atopic dermatitis may be beneficial in DD.
